statement: The roots of $x^{2}-px+q=0$ are $\alpha$ and $\beta$. Express $\alpha^{3}+\beta^{3}$ in terms of $p$ and $q$, and hence find the quadratic whose roots are $\alpha^{3}$ and $\beta^{3}$.
solution: We have $\alpha+\beta=p$ and $\alpha\beta=q$. Then $\alpha^{3}+\beta^{3}=(\alpha+\beta)^{3}-3\alpha\beta(\alpha+\beta)=p^{3}-3pq$. Also $\alpha^{3}\beta^{3}=q^{3}$. The quadratic with roots $\alpha^{3}$ and $\beta^{3}$ has sum $p^{3}-3pq$ and product $q^{3}$, so it is $x^{2}-(p^{3}-3pq)x+q^{3}=0$.
hints: The product of the new roots is q^3.
Form the quadratic from its sum and product of roots.
